extracted.intended_audience: school and college administrators, Title IX coordinators, investigators, decision-makers, and institutional policymakers responsible for Title IX compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Implementation and operation of §106.45 Title IX sexual harassment grievance procedures, including notice/actual-knowledge rules, training, evidentiary evaluation, supportive measures, dismissal rules, appeals, and related recipient obligations. Focused on how institutions must respond to reports and conduct investigations/adjudications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable treatment based on party status (no sex discrimination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions that treat complainants and respondents equitably based on party status, or that apply only to complainants or only to respondents for the purpose of fostering truth-seeking, do not discriminate based on sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department disagrees that a provision conferring a right or protection only to respondents treats complainants inequitably where it helps ensure burden of proof remains on recipient and serves truth-seeking (example: §106.45(b)(1)(iv)). Any person regardless of sex may be complainant or respondent; distinctions based on party status are not sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer supportive measures to each complainant regardless of formal complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer supportive measures to each complainant whether or not the complainant files a formal complaint or otherwise participates in a grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement defers to complainant autonomy to decide whether to participate; supportive measures must be offered promptly and are available even without a formal complaint (see §106.44 and related discussion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartial, truth-seeking grievance process (objective evaluation of evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.45 is premised on accurate resolution of allegations through objective evaluation of all relevant evidence without bias and without prejudgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neither complainants nor respondents are automatically or prematurely believed or disbelieved until credibility determinations are made as part of the grievance process. The process is designed to reach accurate determinations regarding responsibility so victims receive remedies only after reliable determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training to serve impartially and avoid bias/conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX Coordinators, investigators, decision-makers, and any person who facilitates an informal resolution process must receive training on how to serve impartially, including by avoiding prejudgment of the facts, conflicts of interest, and bias (§106.45(b)(1)(iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training requirement is intended to reduce the influence of biases and prejudices from other systems (e.g., criminal justice). The Department expects training to address impartiality, avoidance of conflicts, and recognizing/avoiding bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appealability for conflict of interest or bias (§106.45(b)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Either party may file an appeal on the ground that the Title IX Coordinator, investigator, or decision-maker had a conflict of interest or bias that affected the outcome of the matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals may allege bias for or against complainants or respondents generally, or bias against the individual, and are an explicit remedy to address impartiality concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt response and prohibition of deliberate indifference (§106.44(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must respond promptly to every report of sexual harassment of which the recipient has actual knowledge, and do so in a non-deliberately indifferent manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to respond when the requirements of §106.44(a) are met constitutes deliberate indifference and is a violation. The obligation applies to reports of harassment occurring in the recipient's education program or activity in the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on retaliation (§106.71)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.71 prohibits retaliation against any individual making a report, filing a complaint, or participating in a Title IX investigation or proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retaliation protections apply without bias against an individual's sex, race, ethnicity, or other characteristics; the rule addresses commenters' concerns about retaliation fears and ensures protections for participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient discretion on disciplinary sanctions but must avoid sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department does not prescribe or restrict recipients' discretion regarding whether disciplinary sanctions must be imposed or their proportionality, but actions must not constitute sex discrimination under Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal courts should not second-guess schools' disciplinary decisions; the Department focuses on reliable outcomes and remedies rather than imposing a federal standard of fairness or proportionality for sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible dismissal of a formal complaint (§106.45(b)(3)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient, in its discretion, may dismiss a formal complaint if the complainant notifies the Title IX Coordinator in writing that the complainant wishes to withdraw it, if the respondent is no longer enrolled or employed, or if specific circumstances prevent collecting evidence sufficient to reach a determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declines to add a separate 'reasonable cause' threshold; dismissal grounds are limited to the listed circumstances (e.g., complainant withdrawal, respondent no longer affiliated, or inability to collect sufficient evidence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective evaluation of all relevant evidence (inculpatory and exculpatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators and decision-makers must objectively evaluate all relevant evidence, both inculpatory and exculpatory, free from conflicts of interest or bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While §106.45 does not set parameters for 'quality' of evidence, it requires objective evaluation of all relevant evidence and forbids selective reliance that would undercut reliable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility on qualifications and outsourcing (no attorney requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may carry out §106.45 responsibilities by outsourcing to professionally trained investigators and adjudicators; the Department declines to require Title IX Coordinators, investigators, or decision-makers to be licensed attorneys or to specify minimum qualifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leaving recipients flexibility in appointing personnel makes it more likely recipients can meet obligations; recipients may hire external professionals to perform investigations/adjudications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actual knowledge standard and differentiation by school level (§106.30 and §106.44(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition of 'actual knowledge' is revised to differentiate elementary/secondary schools from postsecondary institutions: notice to any employee of an elementary or secondary school charges the recipient with actual knowledge; for postsecondary institutions, notice to the Title IX Coordinator or an official with authority triggers the obligation to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change reflects expectations about students' abilities to report at different ages and addresses commenters' concerns about barriers to reporting. Recipients can designate additional officials as 'with authority' to expand routes of notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and reporting channels requirement (§106.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must notify all students and employees of the Title IX Coordinator's contact information, prominently display that contact information on the recipient's website, and state that any person may report sexual harassment in person, by mail, telephone, email, or any means resulting in the Title IX Coordinator receiving the report; reports may be made at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement aims to provide clear, accessible reporting channels and ensures complainants and third parties can trigger a recipient's response obligations through multiple, accessible means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing barriers for vulnerable student populations
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies must account for students who face additional barriers to reporting (students with disabilities, immigrant students, international students, transgender and non-binary students, homeless or economically disadvantaged students) and provide accessible reporting options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For elementary/secondary schools, notice to any employee addresses barriers; for postsecondary institutions, notification of Title IX Coordinator contact info and optional institutional mandatory-reporting policies are tools to increase accessibility while preserving student autonomy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient discretion on mandatory reporting policies for postsecondary institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Postsecondary institutions may decide whether to implement universal mandatory reporting policies; the adapted actual knowledge definition permits recipients discretion to determine which employees are mandatory reporters and which may keep disclosures confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach balances survivor autonomy with institutional options to expand mandatory reporters if desired; recipients may also empower as many officials as they wish with authority to institute corrective measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complainant autonomy and confidentiality choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Complainants at postsecondary institutions may confide in employees without automatically triggering institutional response obligations (if those employees are not designated as officials with authority), preserving complainant control over whether to initiate institutional processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students have greater control over whether or when to report; institutions must still notify and inform students of the Title IX Coordinator's role and options for supportive measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to advisor of choice once grievance process initiated
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a grievance process has been initiated, recipients must provide parties with written notice of each party's right to select an advisor of choice; nothing precludes a complainant from bringing a supportive friend to an initial meeting with the Title IX Coordinator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many complainants bring friends or family for support; the written notice requirement ensures parties understand advisor rights during the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: No triage by alleged severity of sexual harassment under §106.45
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department rejects treating cases differently (triaging) based on an asserted severity scale; any type of sexual harassment as defined in §106.30 warrants the §106.45 grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title IX sexual harassment is defined to include three categories of sex-based conduct, each of which constitutes serious behavior likely to deny equal access; thus all such allegations warrant the formal grievance framework rather than a severity-based triage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to offer remedies only after reliable determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX requires recipients to provide victims with remedies designed to restore or preserve access to education, and that obligation can be met only after a reliable determination regarding responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reliable factual determinations are a precondition for appropriate remedies; the grievance process' focus on accurate outcomes is tied to effective provision of remedies.
